CSS Today

Widely supported new features and how to use them.

What is Baseline?

An indicator of whether a feature is safe to use across all major browsers (Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari).

MDN marks every CSS property page with its current Baseline status. CanIUse.com is also a great resource.

All slides in this deck include Baseline features, either Newly or Widely Available.

✓ Widely available

In all major browsers for 30+ months. Safe for any project.

✓ Newly available

Just landed in all major browsers. Usable today, but consider your support window.

⚠ Limited availability

Not yet supported in all major browsers. Use with caution or a fallback.

Interop 2026

A yearly initiative by Apple, Google, Igalia, Microsoft, and Mozilla to improve cross-browser consistency. Each year they select focus areas and work together to fix real-world compatibility issues. This is the fifth year of the project.

CSS focus areas in 2026:

Track progress at wpt.fyi/interop-2026, 20 focus areas total in 2026.

Part 01

Selectors

Modern pseudo-classes that let CSS detect context, content, and user state.

Pseudo-class: :not()

Exclude elements from a selector.

Modern :not() accepts selector lists; the old single-argument version could not. Replaces the pattern of styling the common case then overriding for exceptions.

  • First item
  • Second item
  • Third item
  • Last item

Pseudo-class: :has()

Select elements based on their contents or following siblings.

Avoids toggling classes in JavaScript or adding template conditionals just to reflect content state in CSS.

Card with image

Card without image

Card without image

Pseudo-class: :nth-child(n of .selector)

Target the nth element matching a selector, basically filtering :nth-child by class.

The old :nth-child(2) counted every sibling regardless of type or class, making it nearly useless in real world scenarios.

  • Item 1
  • Item 2 (highlight class)
  • Item 3 (highlight class)
  • Item 4
  • Item 5 (highlight class)

Pseudo-class: :empty

Match elements that have no children, including no text nodes.

Lets CSS react to empty containers from the server or API without any JavaScript.

Has content

Pseudo-class: :focus-visible

Show focus styles only when keyboard-navigated, not on mouse click.

Now the recommended way to style focus indicators, replacing outline: none hacks that remove visibility for keyboard users entirely.



This is a link

Pseudo-class: :user-valid / :user-invalid

Validate only after user interaction; avoids error styles on untouched fields.

Unlike :invalid, they don't fire on page load, so fields don't show red borders before anyone has typed anything.



Part 02

Layout

Sizing, spacing, and layout properties that replace custom calculations and JavaScript-driven patterns.

Concept: logical directions

Logical properties use block, inline, start, and end instead of top/right/bottom/left, so layouts adapt to any writing direction automatically.

In horizontal left-to-right writing: block = vertical axis, inline = horizontal axis. With writing-mode: vertical-rl, the axes swap; logical properties follow automatically.

block-start ↓
→ inline-start
element
inline-end ←
↑ block-end

Property: logical sizing

Use flow-relative sizing instead of width and height.

In horizontal writing, inline-size = width and block-size = height. In vertical writing mode, the roles swap automatically; layouts adapt without extra overrides.

Some text inside the box

Property: logical spacing

Use flow-relative margin, padding, and border shorthands.

inline and block are applied to margin and padding. Physical directions stay fixed; logical ones adapt.

Flow-relative spacing adapts to writing direction.

Value: display: flow-root

Create a block formatting context; contains floats without clearfix hacks.

Fully contains its children, including floated elements. The explicit, readable replacement for clearfix: one property, no side effects, says exactly what it does.

This text flows alongside the float.

Property: aspect-ratio

Maintains a width-to-height ratio as the element scales, without explicit width and height values. No math, no hacks.

Value: fit-content

Size an element to its content, with optional max constraint.

Unlike display: inline-block, it stays in normal flow, so margin-inline: auto still works to center it.

Short text
This is a much longer piece of text that shows how sizing keywords behave differently

Functions: min(), max(), clamp()

Constrain values with comparison functions; no media queries needed.

clamp(min, preferred, max) sets both a floor and a ceiling in one expression. min(min1, min2) sets the minimum value, and max(max1, max2) sets the maximum value.

Resize the browser to see clamping.

Pattern: center a shrink-wrapped element

width: fit-content combined with margin-inline: auto centers a block element that sizes to its content, no hardcoded width, no extra wrapper elements needed.

Centered to content width

Part 03

Typography

Text properties that handle decoration, overflow, and balance, without manual tweaks.

Property: text-*

Style underlines, overlines, and line-throughs with custom color, thickness, and offset.

This is a text decoration example.

Property: text-wrap

Control how text wraps: balance line lengths or avoid orphans.

Designed for headings and pull quotes: anywhere you'd otherwise tweak max-width until the line breaks look right.

A heading with text that wraps unevenly at the end

Part 04

Color & Visual Effects

Mix colors, fade images, blur backgrounds, and adapt to dark mode, all natively in CSS.

Function: color-mix()

Mix two colors in a chosen color space; the space changes the result.

sRGB blending often goes muddy in the middle; OkLCH stays perceptually vivid throughout the blend.

Property: mask-image

Mask an element using a gradient or image.

Black areas are fully visible; transparent areas reveal the background beneath. Creates smooth fade effects without image editing.

Property: backdrop-filter

Apply graphical effects to the area behind an element.

The element needs a semi-transparent background to reveal the effect; a fully opaque element just covers it.

Property: color-scheme

Tell the browser which color schemes an element supports.

Without it, native controls like inputs, checkboxes, and scrollbars render in light mode even inside a fully dark-themed UI.





Property: caret-color

Change the color of the text cursor in inputs and textareas.

A small finishing touch for on-brand form fields. Can also be set to transparent to hide the cursor entirely.

Part 05

Transitions

Animate elements in and out of the page, including discrete properties like display: none.

Property: transition-behavior: allow-discrete

Transition discrete properties like display; previously impossible without JS.

Normally, toggling display instantly removes the element; allow-discrete keeps it visible long enough for the exit transition to finish, then hides it.

I fade out on hide

At-rule: @starting-style

Define initial styles for enter transitions; enables CSS-only enter animations. Requires transition-behavior: allow-discrete.

Without it, elements going from hidden to visible snap in instantly at full opacity; @starting-style gives the browser a starting point to animate from.

I animate in AND out

Part 06

Container Queries

Style components based on their own size, not the viewport; replaces ResizeObserver and duplicate templates.

At-rule: @container

Apply styles based on the container's size, not the viewport.

Mark a parent with container-type: inline-size, then write @container () {} rules that respond to that parent's available width.

Card adapts to its container
